title: One-seed RESET-relative deployed-array pulse recovery pilot
hypothesis: Teacher-KL updates expressed through physical single-pulse writes can recover validation accuracy from a frozen nine-level RESET-relative QAT deployment, and a Tiki-Taka accumulator can use the same slow-array pulse budget more effectively than direct stochastic writes.
motivation: The completed RESET-relative quantized-HWA study transferred much better than the earlier cell-specific mapping but still showed a material deployed-array gap. This pilot starts every arm from one freshly commissioned and pulse-programmed development array, then compares a no-gradient rail-refresh control, direct stochastic SET/RESET updates, ideal-fast Tiki-Taka, and a fully physical repaired-OM fast-pair Tiki-Taka path. It is explicitly a one-seed mechanism and implementation pilot, not formal evidence. The hidden persistent endpoint is retained only as the device update state and diagnostic; apparent-forward accuracy remains the deployment headline.

completion_criteria: Before any recovery run, produce exactly one fresh pulse-resolved source deployment from checkpoint SHA-256 537681598b887d4d63c6429c7f7bee3a7082041215c09d6cb3c25947452f311a on counterfactual-repaired assignment seed 84501 and endpoint seed 84601. Bind the source checkpoint selection epoch 4, teacher SHA-256 9a961a77628e365b54fdf59304ec7fddf46f1f4834c4c03cecea9c204f837f52, and device-model SHA-256 3030e04d6205dc90d0894ac453d2c1c522dffdc004f69b9c6ab7eaf7ef4b8ba3.

Every recovery arm must validate and reuse the exact source deployment bytes, embedded population fingerprint, saved raw apparent endpoint, clipped apparent endpoint, persistent endpoint, RESET baselines, requested targets, and post-programming RNG continuation. It may not reprogram, remap, resample, inspect hidden bounds to choose an update, or substitute another slow array.

Run exactly one seed for each of the twelve method-by-budget cells: rail refresh, direct pulse, ideal-fast Tiki-Taka, and physical-fast Tiki-Taka crossed with 0.1, 1, and 4 requested slow pulses per slow cell. Each arm runs the fixed ten epochs and 34,380 minibatch steps and is retained at epoch 10 without validation selection.

All arms use the same teacher-KL gradients and frozen QAT learning rates. Rail refresh computes no gradients. Direct stochastic writes calibrate one positive probability scale on exactly 64 replayed source-state minibatches without consuming the training permutation. Tiki-Taka visits each slow column cyclically and spreads the declared number of column visits evenly over all steps.

A slow write is one physical OM SET or RESET pulse on the individual selected conductance. Never project back to a code level, round an endpoint, clip the persistent plant, or silently exceed the whole-run cap of 15,880, 158,800, or 635,200 slow-pulse requests. Record SET, RESET, state-changing, saturated, clipped-apparent, layer, and unique-cell counts.

The physical-fast Tiki-Taka arms sample exactly one repaired assignment 85501 with two fast cells per slow conductance, use endpoint seed 85601, commission paired rails from eight RESET/read samples and a three-standard-error guarded pair maximum, equalize by verify, accumulate with physical SET pulses, and adaptively RESET each transferred pair slice. Retain all fast population, commissioning, SET/RESET, verify, reversal, failure, and RNG state.

At initialization and after every epoch, fit a positive logit gain on the fixed 1,024-example training calibration cohort and evaluate both apparent and persistent states at the original gain and recalibrated gain on all 5,000 validation examples. Positive gain must leave each state's argmax accuracy exactly invariant. Persistent-state accuracy is a hidden-state diagnostic, not a retention or fresh-read measurement.

Every epoch boundary must resume exactly, including slow and fast apparent/persistent arrays, all generator streams, direct scale, ideal accumulator, cyclic transfer position, pulse ledgers, data permutation, global step, calibration gain, and metric history. Preserve source and terminal endpoint bundles even if accuracy degrades.

The pilot is complete only when the source deployment and all twelve recovery runs pass artifact-hash verification. Do not release a formal test array, add seeds, select a favorable budget, or update the experimental manifest before the one-seed mechanism results are reviewed.
analysis_plan: First prove that all twelve initialization records have the same apparent and persistent accuracy, KL, endpoints, source deployment digest, and source gain. Treat any mismatch as an implementation failure rather than a result.

For each arm report terminal apparent-forward validation accuracy minus its identical initialization, the best observed trajectory only as a descriptive diagnostic, persistent-state diagnostic change, KL change, calibrated gain trajectory, requested/state-changing slow pulses, saturation, clipping, code crossings, sign flips, and unique cells touched.

Within each 0.1, 1, and 4 budget compare direct pulses against ideal-fast Tiki-Taka and physical-fast Tiki-Taka. Use rail refresh to distinguish gradient-directed recovery from merely rewriting cells toward their original target rail. Do not interpret a single stochastic seed as a method ranking.

For physical versus ideal Tiki-Taka separate fast-array loss into commissioning/equalization failures, stochastic gradient accumulation, transfer probability, adaptive reset cost/failure, and slow-pulse outcomes. Report fast costs separately from the matched slow-array budget.

Advance only if at least one gradient-directed arm improves terminal apparent accuracy over the shared initialization without violating caps or resume determinism. Then freeze the method and budget before running two additional development repeats and a separately declared formal deployment study.
